auth.description:
#
# Credentials seeded into authup at boot. Empty passwords are generated once and
# kept stable across upgrades via lookup.
# GITOPS WARNING: lookup is inert under `helm template` and ArgoCD-style
# renders — every sync would then apply a NEW random value, roll the pods via
# the checksum annotation, and desync the Secret from the live credential
# (authup only applies the admin password at first provisioning unless the
# reset flag is set). GitOps users MUST set explicit values or auth.existingSecret.

adminPassword.description:
Initial admin user password ("" = generate once, keep across upgrades).
Changing it after the first install only takes effect with
adminPasswordReset=true for one upgrade cycle
adminPassword.title: adminPassword

adminPasswordReset.description: Re-assert the admin password on every boot (USER_ADMIN_PASSWORD_RESET)
adminPasswordReset.title: adminPasswordReset

existingSecret.description: Existing secret holding the keys below instead of the chart-managed secret (tpl-rendered)
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

adminPasswordKey.description: Key inside the (existing) secret holding the admin password
adminPasswordKey.title: adminPasswordKey

secretsEncryptionKeyKey.description: Key inside the (existing) secret holding the secrets encryption key
secretsEncryptionKeyKey.title: secretsEncryptionKeyKey

systemClientSecretKey.description: Key inside the (existing) secret holding the system client secret
systemClientSecretKey.title: systemClientSecretKey

secretsEncryptionKey.description:
Optional AES-256 key-encryption-key wrapping the realm key store
(SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY, base64-encoded 32 bytes). Deliberately never
generated by the chart: this key is effectively write-once — losing or
rotating it bricks wrapped MFA seeds and signing keys. Set it explicitly
here, or reference it via existingSecret plus
secretsEncryptionKeyEnabled=true, and back it up.
secretsEncryptionKey.title: secretsEncryptionKey

secretsEncryptionKeyEnabled.description:
Declare that auth.existingSecret carries the secrets encryption key
(under secretKeys.secretsEncryptionKeyKey). Required for the key to be
wired from an existing secret — it is never inferred, so a missing key can
not silently fail open into plaintext-at-rest
secretsEncryptionKeyEnabled.title: secretsEncryptionKeyEnabled

systemClientEnabled.description: Provision the built-in system client (CLIENT_SYSTEM_ENABLED); required for machine-to-machine consumers
systemClientEnabled.title: systemClientEnabled

systemClientSecret.description: System client secret ("" = generate once when systemClientEnabled)
systemClientSecret.title: systemClientSecret

systemClientSecretReset.description: Re-assert the system client secret on every boot (CLIENT_SYSTEM_SECRET_RESET)
systemClientSecretReset.title: systemClientSecretReset
